title: Accuracy and Political Bias of News Source Credibility Ratings by Large Language Models

paper.venue: Proceedings of the 17th ACM Web Science Conference (WebSci '25), pp. 127-137; final-version text of arXiv 2304.00228 used here
paper.third_party_repos_in_scaffold: github.com/jujumilk3/leaked-system-prompts is only a citation (footnote 13), not the paper's artifact

dependence.note: All results are the nine LLMs' own credibility ratings. The full set of 140,148 LLM responses (rating + explanation) is released in data/llm_ratings.parquet together with the query code, so the original outputs can be re-scored without any API call (L1-level artifact).

claim.statement: In the default (no partisan role) configuration, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09's 0-1 credibility ratings of news domains correlate only moderately with human expert ratings - Spearman rho = 0.54 on the 3,077 domains rated by all nine LLMs (rho = 0.62 on the 4,422 domains it rated; Figure 3, 'GPT-4' row/column) - while inter-LLM agreement is high (mean rho = 0.79); and, unlike every other non-o1 model, GPT-4 shows no statistically significant liberal bias in the default configuration (Figure 6, t-test of LLM-rating-bias scores on left- vs right-leaning sources, p >= 0.05). It declines to rate (returns -1) 41.2% of the 7,523 domains.
claim.metric: Spearman rank correlation between LLM rating (0-1, -1 excluded) and Lin et al. aggregate expert rating (pc1), computed (a) on domains rated by all LLMs and (b) on the pairwise intersection; political bias = t-statistic of a t-test comparing (LLM rating - expert rating) on left- vs right-leaning sources (Robertson et al. audience scores, threshold 0)

original_values.default_config_political_bias: not significant (Figure 6; exact t-statistic not printed in text)

recomputed_from_released_data_by_card_au.note: recomputed from data/llm_ratings.parquet x hauselin/domain-quality-ratings/data/domain_pc1.csv; matches Figure 3 after rounding

claim.original_source: Figure 3 heatmap values and Sections 4.2/4.3 of the paper; data/llm_ratings.parquet + data/README.md in repo (model code gpt4turbo20240409 = gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)

protocol.model_status: dying, OpenAI shutdown 2026-10-23 (target_models.json); verified as an experimental arm in Section 3.1 and data/README.md
protocol.prompt_source: code/prompt_factory.py (SYS_BASE, SYS_IDENTITY, USER_INSTRUCTION, USER_FORMAT) and Section 3.2 + Appendix of the paper

messages.content: You are an assistant to determine the credibility of websites.  [+ ' You identify as {a Democrat|an Independent|a Republican} on the US political spectrum.' for the partisan-role arms]

USER_INSTRUCTION.format(domain=<domain>) + ' ' + USER_FORMAT  (rate credibility 0-1, -1 if unknown, short explanation; JSON schema {url, rating, explanation}; 'Only return the JSON object, nothing else.')

params.max_tokens: not set for the OpenAI client (2046 only for the together.ai client)
params.other: safety filters disabled only for Gemini

protocol.n_items: 7,523 domains (Lin et al. list intersected with the Tranco Sept-2022 top-5.5M); partisan-role arms use the 2,683-domain subset with Robertson et al. bias scores
protocol.evaluation: Automatic. Parse JSON (json_repair) -> rating in [0,1] or -1 (code/parse_results.py); drop -1; Spearman rho vs expert pc1 on (a) the domain set rated by all models and (b) the pairwise intersection; bias score = LLM rating - expert rating; t-test left vs right sources. Figures 3-8 analysis code is NOT in the repo (only query + parse) and must be re-implemented (simple).
protocol.environment_check: Re-score the released parquet with our re-implemented analysis first: must reproduce rho = 0.54/0.62 and the 41.2% unrated share before any new API call (separates analysis drift from model drift).

artifacts.data_path: external/repos/W4362598103/osome-iu__llm_domain_rating/data/llm_ratings.parquet (140,148 rows; the 7,523-domain list is recoverable from it); expert ratings: external/repos/W4362598103/hauselin__domain-quality-ratings/data/domain_pc1.csv (11,520 domains, cloned); political-bias scores: Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/QAN5VX (not downloaded)
artifacts.eval_path: external/repos/W4362598103/osome-iu__llm_domain_rating/code/parse_results.py (parsing only; correlation/bias analysis not in repo)
artifacts.data_license: repo MIT; LLM outputs released under the repo license; Lin et al. ratings (GitHub, license to check in that repo); Robertson et al. scores under Dataverse terms; Tranco list free
artifacts.notes: Released LLM ratings allow a zero-cost analysis-only baseline; the Figure 3 numbers were reproduced by the card author from the released data.

blockers: Figure-level analysis code (Spearman/t-test/aggregation) not in the repo - must be re-implemented (low risk, done once for the environment check)
Robertson et al. political-bias scores must be fetched from Harvard Dataverse under its terms (needed only for the bias half of the claim)
Domain-knowledge drift: the 2022 Tranco-based domain list contains now-defunct sites, so the -1 refusal share is expected to move for reasons unrelated to model change

baseline_alive.purpose: live-arm baseline (P0), default configuration on all 7,523 domains

llama (open weights, e.g. Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, weights hash fixed)

budget.assumptions: default configuration only (covers both halves of the claim): 7,523 calls x 3 seeds; ~200 input tokens/call (system + instruction + JSON-format block), ~80 output tokens/call (JSON with ~200-char explanation; measured mean 202 chars in the released data). Temperature 0 -> a single seed (~$33) is arguably sufficient; the three partisan-role arms would add 8,049 calls (~$35) per seed.

user_checks: Confirm the core-claim choice: default-configuration accuracy (rho 0.54/0.62) + absence of default liberal bias, rather than the partisan-role steering effect (Figure 6, all models).
Temperature 0 in the original: accept 1 seed (~$33) instead of 3 seeds (~$99)?
OK to download the Robertson et al. political-bias scores from Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/QAN5VX) under its terms of use? (Lin et al. ratings already cloned from GitHub.)
domain_notes: The 'human expert' reference is an ensemble (Lin et al. 2023) of six rating sources such as NewsGuard and MBFC - a contested, time-varying ground truth, so absolute rho values should be read relative to inter-LLM agreement. The domain list is a Sept-2022 Tranco intersection; defunct sites inflate refusals. Political leaning comes from audience-sharing scores (Robertson et al.), not content analysis. The o1-mini and Gemini 1.5 arms are dead; the Llama 3.1 arms were served by together.ai.
